proposals.title: Give the parked spec-session pool a constraint discriminator — today an UNCONSTRAINED request pays a ~16 ms draft-graph recapture because a constrained one ran before it
proposals.mechanism: NEITHER SIDE — scheduler/graph-identity only, zero numeric change. The draft-mask node's presence is a capture-time shape: `dctx.graph_masked != dmask_on` drops the parked graph and clears the keeper (crates/memra-engine/src/spec.rs:6228-6232), and `graph_masked` is set at capture (spec.rs:6271). But `DraftGraphCtx` is parked on the `SpecSession` (spec.rs:8461-8463) and pooled across requests keyed only on `PoolKey = (model, cache_ns)` (worker.rs:980, worker.rs:6837) with no constraint field, and the park path has no constraint filter at all (worker.rs:6217-6240). Meanwhile a constrained request can never resume (`let resumed = if constraint.is_some() { None }`, worker.rs:7332). Net effect today: a tool-call/JSON request parks a `graph_masked=true` ctx, and the next unconstrained request that extends that prefix resumes it, mismatches, and pays a full draft-graph recapture — the ~16 ms/burst class the code itself measures (spec.rs:482-486). Fix: either add the mask capability to the park/resume key so a masked ctx is only resumed by a masked request, or refuse to park a `graph_masked=true` ctx (constrained requests cannot resume it anyway, so parking it is pure liability). One-line-class change plus a metrics counter for how often the drop fires.
proposals.expected_gain: Removes a ~16 ms recapture from the TTFT of the unconstrained request that happens to follow tool-call traffic on the same prefix. Small per event, but it is on the money path (mixed tool + chat traffic on one cache namespace) and the fix has no measurable cost. Also removes a wasted `d_vocab/32`-word device buffer and one `alloc_u32_zeroed` from the resumed session.
proposals.risk: Very low. The refuse-to-park variant slightly reduces pool hit rate for constrained sessions — but they cannot resume from the pool at all (worker.rs:7332), so the reduction is exactly zero. The keyed variant needs the discriminator to be the same predicate the engine tests (`constraint.draft_mask_enabled()`, spec.rs:6220), not `constraint.is_some()`, or the mismatch survives. Gate: tools/serve-smoke.sh plus a new mixed constrained-then-unconstrained cell asserting no `graph_masked` drop and byte-identical unconstrained output; accept-gate text_sha256 must not move (it is not a numeric change).
proposals.evidence: crates/memra-engine/src/spec.rs:6222-6232 and :6271 (drop + set of graph_masked); crates/memra-engine/src/spec.rs:8461-8463 (ctx parked on the session); crates/memra-engine/src/spec.rs:482-486 (~16 ms/burst recapture class); crates/memra-server/src/worker.rs:980 and :6837 (PoolKey has no constraint field); crates/memra-server/src/worker.rs:6217-6240 (park path, no constraint filter); crates/memra-server/src/worker.rs:7332 (constrained requests never resume)

proposals.title: Coverage-escape telemetry for the Qwen d2t draft head, plus a load-time `.learned` rank sidecar — the instrument every trim decision is currently missing, and the cheapest form of the adaptive-trim win
proposals.mechanism: DRAFT SIDE ONLY, and numerically inert at serve time. A coverage escape (a token the target emits that has no d2t row, hence a guaranteed rejection) is the ENTIRE measured cost of the trim, yet nothing counts it: `grep -rn 'TrimAdapt|trim_adapt' --include='*.rs' crates/ | grep -v gemma_spec.rs` returns zero hits, `MtpHead.d2t` is a plain immutable `Option<Vec<u32>>` with no `present` bitmap (hybrid.rs:794-795), and gemma's own `maybe_add` bool return — the only thing that distinguishes 'was an escape' from 'already present' — is discarded by all three callers (gemma_spec.rs:117-119). Add (a) a host `present` bitmap built once from `d2t` at load (248 KB for a 248320 vocab), (b) an escape counter + bounded escaped-id set incremented in the verify commit walk where the emitted target ids are already in hand (spec.rs:7963-7996 / the same place the accept walk runs), (c) an `escapes`/`escape_rate` field on the per-request spec usage and /metrics — today `gram_cuts` and draft-mask timings are stderr `eprintln!` only (spec.rs:8427-8433, worker.rs:9200-9209) and metrics.rs has zero hits for them, and (d) the cold-learn half of gemma's mechanism: append escaped ids to `<ranks>.learned` at process exit and pre-fill them into the gather at the NEXT load, exactly as gemma_spec.rs:129-149 + :294-316 do. Cold-learn deliberately does NOT mutate the trim set inside a live process, so the trim is constant for the process lifetime and there is exactly one numeric program per request — it dodges the sampled-spec hazard that in-flight learning carries.
proposals.expected_gain: The instrument itself is what makes every other trim/rank decision measurable, including the 3.8 day-one rank corpus: the two documented ways to lose 10-15 acceptance points (wrong chat template, wrong corpus mix) both show up as an escape-rate spike and are otherwise INVISIBLE — a 10.9% structurally-unproposable rate was found only by a bespoke offline analysis. proposals.title: Prompt-conditioned escape rows: a per-SESSION draft-head tail gathered from the request's own prompt ids — the parked 'prompt-adaptive trim' lane, restructured so the trim set is fixed per request
proposals.mechanism: DRAFT SIDE ONLY. The parked lane's own trigger evidence: escapees are prompt-domain content words, and an oracle that injected the 13 exact escapee ids flipped a -17% cell to +2% AT IDENTICAL ACCEPTANCE. The lane was parked because it 'needs per-request head regather or resident-row masking, a memory-contract change'. The restructure that makes it affordable: keep the shared trim head as-is and add a small PER-SESSION tail — `esc_head` of n_esc rows (e.g. 1024) plus `esc_d2t: Vec<u32>` living beside `DraftGraphCtx` on the `SpecSession`, filled ONCE at session start from the prompt's distinct ids that are not already `present` in d2t. The draft head forward issues its existing qmatvec into `logits[0..d_vocab]` and a second into `logits[d_vocab..d_vocab+n_esc]`; argmax runs over the concatenation and an index >= d_vocab maps through `esc_d2t`. Because `DraftGraphCtx` is already per-session (spec.rs:8461-8463) and the buffers are per-session and never realloc'd, both calls capture cleanly and there is no cross-session row collision — which is the failure the process-global gemma `TrimAdapt` would have had here. Crucially the tail is a function of the REQUEST'S OWN PROMPT, not of load history, so the numeric program is fixed for the whole request and a fixed (seed, prompt, K) still reproduces its stream: this is the design point that keeps `MEMRA_SPEC_TEMP`'s seeded-reproducibility gate intact, which an incrementally-learning trim would break (under sampled spec the draft q lives on the trimmed vocab and enters the Leviathan/Chen accept decision, spec.rs:5966-5970, :7919-7924).
proposals.expected_gain: The oracle bound on the cell it was built for: -17% -> +2.5% at identical acceptance, and 'trim >= untrimmed on EVERY measured cell'. Translated to the 3.8 swap, the value is not a headline percentage but the removal of the per-cell fear that currently forces cells to be served UNTRIMMED (gemma 31B short is shipped untrimmed for exactly this reason) — i.e. it is what lets a day-one 3.8 ship trimmed everywhere with the trim's +2.8-10.5% e2e instead of cell-by-cell.
proposals.risk: Highest-effort item here and the one with a genuine numerical wrinkle: for the shipped EXTERNAL drafter the trim head is NVFP4 (2880 B/row) while the only available source of arbitrary rows is the trunk's Q5_K output.weight (3520 B/row), so the tail block is a DIFFERENT quantization of the same underlying matrix. Two blocks quantized differently means the cross-block argmax comparison carries a small systematic bias — proposal-side only (it can shift which token is proposed, never what is emitted), but it must be measured, not assumed, and it is a reason to prefer the self-trim arm (MEMRA_FRSPEC_TRIM gathers rows from the trunk's own head, hybrid.rs:1555-1570, so tail and trim share a dtype). VRAM: n_esc=1024 at 5440 B/row = 5.6 MB/session, ~22 MB at the 4-session demote threshold. Also the shipped external drafter file carries no full-vocab head to gather from (its output.weight is already (5120, 32768)), so the trunk-source route or the self-trim arm is mandatory. Gate: accept-gate.sh (spec counts move, text_sha256 must NOT), run-spec K=1..8 self-consistency, run-gen argmax MATCH, plus a seeded-sampled reproducibility cell run twice under different concurrency to prove the per-request tail is load-history-independent.

proposals.title: Auto-derived tool-call scaffolding draft mask: extend the proven draft-mask mechanism to `tools` traffic, which is grammar-FREE today — via a draft-only advisor seam, never through `s.constraint`
proposals.mechanism: DRAFT SIDE ONLY, and it must stay that way by construction. Today `tools` requests are completely unconstrained: tool schemas render into the template's own `<tools>` branch (worker.rs:6599) and the emitted `<tool_call>` blocks are only PARSED back (toolcall.rs:19 — 'It is PARSING ONLY ... never touches generation'); `s.constraint` is built solely from `response_format` (worker.rs:354, main.rs:898-903). So the entire tool-call class — the class routers gate and rank separately, and which one gateway requires outright — gets zero benefit from a mechanism that was worth +5.0% e2e and 0.561 -> 0.651 acceptance on tight schemas. Yet inside a `<tool_call>` block the emission is a rigid template law with the function and parameter names drawn from the request's OWN schemas (toolcall.rs:1-30, OPEN/CLOSE/`<function=`/`<parameter=`). Build a tiny DFA over that law, driven by the same state machine toolcall.rs already runs, and expose ONLY the draft-side half of the hook: `draft_mask_enabled`/`draft_begin`/`draft_mask_words`/`draft_advance` (spec.rs:200-220), returning `None` (= unmasked, existing fallback) everywhere outside a scaffolding region so free prose and argument VALUES are never touched. This must be a NEW draft-only seam, not `s.constraint`, for three independently fatal reasons: (1) `SpecConstraint::mask_logits` is applied to the TARGET's logits at prime and at the cut slot (spec.rs:5874, :7993) — that IS an emission change; (2) `constraint.is_some()` disables pool resume entirely (worker.rs:7332), so every tool request would lose continuation reuse; (3) the engine hard-refuses constrained + sampled spec (spec.rs:5501-5503), so tool traffic at temperature > 0 would fall out of spec altogether. PREREQUISITE inside this proposal: `upload_draft_mask` is unmetered and expensive per DRAFT POSITION — a full-target-vocab bitset `to_vec()` (~31 KB at a 248k vocab), a fresh `vec![0u32; words]`, an O(d_vocab) permute (32768 iterations), a full all-zero scan, and a pageable H2D (spec.rs:243-265, lib.rs:4342-4347). At K=3 that is 3x/round of unmetered host work on the critical path, and it becomes hot the moment the mask runs on tool traffic. Fix with a pinned staging buffer, OR-accumulation during the permute (kills the separate all-zero scan), and the position-0 reuse the code's own stale comment already claims but never does (constrained.rs:682-689).
proposals.expected_gain: The draft-mask receipt on a bounded tight schema: gram_cuts -> 0/N, acceptance 0.561 -> 0.651, 216.6 -> 227.5 tok/s (+5.0%). Tool-call scaffolding is the same shape of problem (a small legal set the drafter routinely misses), applied to a class that currently gets nothing. Commercial multiplier: OpenRouter gates tool routing in an insufficient-data tier until 200 tool requests/2h, so tool-path throughput is a listing/ranking gate, not just a latency number.
proposals.risk: THIS IS THE ONE PROPOSAL HERE THAT IS NOT A PROVABLE SUPERSET, and the distinction matters. A user grammar mask can only ever remove GUARANTEED REJECTIONS: under greedy constrained verify the emitted token is always grammar-legal (spec.rs:7972-7996), so an illegal proposal could never have been accepted, and a legal unmasked argmax survives masking unchanged — hence 'never worse'. A derived template-law mask loses that property, because toolcall.rs's own policy explicitly ALLOWS a malformed emission ('surfaced VERBATIM as content ... Never an error'), so the target may emit outside the derived set and a masked position becomes a rejection that would have been an acceptance. Downside is bounded to acceptance (verify still decides emission; the all-zero fallback drafts unmasked, spec.rs:262-264 -> :6936-6941) but it is real and must be measured per class, both rigs. Second risk: the published draft-mask numbers are 9B, GGUF, 5090, c=1 only — there is no 27B, no ST, and no PRO 6000 cell for this mechanism at all, so it sets a one-rig expectation until re-measured. Third: there is NO standing gate — `grep -rn DRAFT_MASK tools/` returns zero hits and serve-smoke.sh has no response_format/grammar cell — so this work must land its gate INSIDE the standing battery, per the H100-lane law that gates outside the battery rot silently. Gate: accept-gate text_sha256 unchanged on a tools cell, mask-on == mask-off byte-identical on greedy tool cells, plus a malformed-emission cell proving the fallback.

proposals.title: Sweep trim SIZE and pad-slot composition — the one trim axis that has never been measured, and the 20k pad slots are not the free space they look like
proposals.mechanism: ARTIFACT-LEVEL, draft side only (which rows the draft head can propose; the emitted stream is the verify's). Every trim receipt in the repo, on every model, is at topN = 32768 — the default is hardcoded in three places (trim_draft_head.py:37, make-trimmed-draft.sh:18, the DRAFT-REGIME build command) and grepping rig5090.jsonl for other sizes returns nothing. Meanwhile own-gen corpora see only 10.5k-12.8k DISTINCT ids, so ~20k of the 32768 slots are `d2t.rs:41-42` pad — 'ascending unseen ids'. The sweep is three artifacts (e.g. 8192 / 16384 / 32768) from the SAME ranks file, measured interleaved x5 on both rigs across the three accept-ref prompt classes plus a cached-long cell. Second arm, more interesting than shrinking: REPLACE the pad rule. Pad currently spends 20k slots covering a contiguous low-id band, which is a coverage asset (one of the 13 known gemma escapees, id 30815, sits inside it) but an arbitrary one; candidate replacements are a second-tier frequency prior from a broader corpus, or the union of the tokenizer's byte-fallback and structural ids. Third arm, if the size curve is steep: a two-tier head (argmax over a hot slice first, full trimmed head only when the hot max is below a confidence threshold) — the per-draft-step dtoh sync it needs already has precedent in the shipped `MEMRA_SPEC_PMIN_INROUND` default.
proposals.expected_gain: Head-read bytes are a measured multi-percent lever: the 248320 -> 32768 trim was worth +10.5% e2e on 27B p2 at slightly HIGHER acceptance (95.6 tok/s @ 72.0% vs 86.5 @ 71.1%), and a separate cell records '+2.6 tok/s' from a 5x drop in draft lm_head reads. A further 2-4x cut of the head is a plausible further few percent IF acceptance holds — and the value of running the sweep is symmetric: a flat or negative curve retires the question and justifies the shipped 32768 with evidence instead of inheritance.
proposals.risk: Not an obvious win, and the reason is specific: shrinking the trim removes pad coverage of a low-id band that demonstrably contains real escapees, so acceptance can fall while speed rises. That interacts with draft-mask too — when no trimmed row is grammar-legal the mask goes DEAD for the rest of the chain and drafting continues unmasked (spec.rs:262-264 -> :6936-6941), so a smaller trim degrades the mask and the trim together on tight schemas. Trim sign is also MODEL-DEPENDENT (27B +3-4%, 9B -5%, E4B untrimmed) and there is an unreconciled acceptance-sign disagreement between the rig5090 cells and the PRO-6000 depth study (nv-trim 0.511 vs nv-full 0.559 short-ctx, yet trim wins e2e on all 16 depth cells) — the two used different drafter shapes, so this sweep should also close that. Pure GPU wall-clock cost, serialized behind one lock per CLAUDE.md's no-parallel-cards law. Gate: accept-gate per artifact (spec counts move, text_sha256 must not), run-spec K=1..8, plus the escape counter from the telemetry proposal so the acceptance delta is attributable to coverage rather than guessed at.

proposals.title: Suffix/prompt-lookup candidate-set mask injected through the EXISTING in-graph draft-mask node — the cheap realization of the survey's Rank 3, aimed at the cached-long shape where acceptance is worst
proposals.mechanism: DRAFT SIDE ONLY. The survey ranks suffix decoding third and prices it as a new 'engine proposer seam (external token proposals into the existing verify/accept path) + suffix-tree state', effort L. The cheaper realization: the draft-mask lane already built everything a candidate SET needs — the `mask_logits_col` in-graph node between the head matmul and the argmax/gumbel/p-min read (spec.rs:2244-2249, :2791-2797), the d2t permutation for trimmed heads (spec.rs:246-252), the contents-only per-replay upload that keeps the capture valid, the all-zero fallback to unmasked drafting, and a kernel-check bit-identity arm (kernel_check.rs:726-761). So instead of a new proposer, build a per-session suffix index over (prompt tokens + committed output) and, at each draft position, mask the draft head to the small set of continuations the suffix match predicts — the head's own logits still choose among them. Keep the mask on ONLY while the match statistic is strong (their max_spec_factor heuristic) and return `None` otherwise, which lands on the existing 'draft unmasked, exactly pre-lane behaviour, never worse' path. Reuses the same draft-only advisor seam as the tool-scaffolding proposal, so the two share their plumbing. Note precisely what this can and cannot buy: a mask bans AFTER the head matmul, so it buys ACCEPTANCE only and saves zero head bytes — shrinking the head is the trim's job, not the mask's.
proposals.expected_gain: Aimed squarely at the declared money shape, which is also the worst-acceptance shape measured: on the rented PRO 6000, q27 cached-long acceptance is 66.36% at K=2, 45.06% at K=3 and 28.30% at K=5, versus cold-long 79.00/77.78/60.00% — the cached-extension class is where the drafter collapses with depth, and it is exactly the input-grounded/repetitive regime where the published PLD and suffix-decoding classes are largest (PLD ~2.4x on input-grounded tasks, 1.56x Spec-Bench overall; suffix decoding 1.8-4.5x e2e in production on SWE-Bench subtasks). Even a partial recovery of cached-long K=3 acceptance toward the cold-long 77.8% is a large e2e move on the shape the business is built on.
proposals.risk: NOT a provable superset, and this is the criterion that separates it from the grammar mask: the grammar mask can only remove tokens the verify could never emit, so it is monotone-non-harmful; a suffix-predicted set can exclude the target's argmax, turning acceptances into rejections. Downside is bounded (proposal-side, verify still decides emission, all-zero -> unmasked fallback) but the sign is genuinely open and workload-dependent, so this needs both-rig, per-class A/B before any default, and the honest failure mode is 'flat on freeform, positive on input-grounded' — the survey's own stated blocker. It also inherits the per-position host cost of `upload_draft_mask` (~31 KB copy + 32768-iteration permute + pageable H2D, all unmetered today) on EVERY request rather than only constrained ones, so the cost fix from the tool-scaffolding proposal is a hard prerequisite here, not an optional cleanup. Reject-my-own-idea note: there is no free provable superset for unconstrained decoding to fall back on — the one target-side fact known at draft time is the target's next-token prediction, and that is already consumed as the carried `next_pred`/bonus token, so it covers no position the chain still has to guess. Gate: accept-gate text_sha256 unchanged on greedy cells (spec counts will move), run-spec K=1..8, run-gen argmax MATCH, and a cached-long serve cell measured on both the 5090 and a PRO 6000.

proposals.title: Escape + pad-hit counters in SpecTelemetry — the missing instrument that makes every trim decision decidable, at zero numeric cost
proposals.mechanism: Build a reverse membership bitset once at load (`MtpHead.present: Vec<u64>`, n_vocab/64 = 31 KB) alongside the existing `d2t: Option<Vec<u32>>` (hybrid.rs:794-795). In the verify round, after the accept decision is already on host, the `bonus` token is the ONE token the draft did not propose; `!present[bonus]` means the draft head has NO ROW for it, so that round's truncation was STRUCTURALLY GUARANTEED — a coverage escape, precisely discriminated from an ordinary mispredict. Add three u64 counters to `SpecTelemetry` (spec.rs:351-364) and thread them through `delta_since` (371-383), `merge` (384-392), and the existing per-model JSON at main.rs:2329-2345: `escape_rounds` (bonus not in trim), `escape_truncating` (that AND n_acc < k_round = the actual loss), and `pad_hits` (accepted draft whose trim row index >= the own-gen observed prefix — i.e. how often the pad tail is a live argmax winner at all). Hook point is one line: `t.record_round(k_round, n_acc)` at spec.rs:8063. Cost is one bitset lookup per ROUND. This is read-only on an already-computed host value — it changes nothing emitted, so it is NOT a numeric-class change, and it is arch-generic (any head with a d2t), not gemma-only.
proposals.expected_gain: No tok/s. It converts 'coverage escapes are the entire trim cost' from a 2026-07-19 gemma oracle claim into a per-model serve-time number on /metrics, on the traffic actually served. Today gram_cuts/acceptance-collapse diagnosis is stderr-only (spec.rs:8427-8433, worker.rs:9200-9209) with zero /metrics fields — so on 3.8 day one an escape-driven acceptance collapse is invisible. `pad_hits` alone decides proposal 2 for free: pad_hits==0 means the 22,147 pad rows never win an argmax and swapping them is risk-free by measurement; pad_hits>0 sizes the risk.
proposals.risk: Near-zero exactness risk (host-side counter, no device work, no emission path). The real risk is scope creep into a per-request usage field; keep it operator-scope /metrics only (main.rs:2327 `metrics_scope.operator()`). Caught by: `kernel-check` unaffected, and a new assertion in tools/serve-smoke.sh that the field is present and non-negative after the spec-vs-plain cell — which also plants the first standing serving-shape check for this lane (today `grep -rn DRAFT_MASK tools/` = 0 hits).
